mainTopic: רב הונא on awareness for half a שיעור; רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש on when discoveries split one חטאת into two, and at what stage they argue
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge on the משנה about eating two half-olive amounts: the רישא, one type in one dish, seems too obvious to teach. רב הונא answers that the person became aware of his sin in between the two halves. The משנה follows רבן גמליאל, who holds that awareness of half a שיעור means nothing, so the halves still combine. Then a new topic begins: someone ate two כזיתים of חלב in one lapse of awareness and found out about each one at a different time. רבי יוחנן says he brings two חטאות and ריש לקיש says one, and each brings a פסוק and explains away the other's פסוק. רבינא asks רב אשי whether they argue before הפרשה, after הפרשה, or in both cases. רב אשי says both, and proves it from how each side explained the other's פסוק. The גמרא rejects that proof, since those explanations may have been conditional 'if you say' answers. Finally עולא begins a new statement about אשם ודאי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first case of the משנה seems too obvious
steps.stepSummary: Since the סיפא (which exempts) was explained as one type in two separate dishes, the רישא must be one type in one dish. But that case is so obvious it hardly needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: This proves that the first part of the משנה is about one type of food in one dish. But one type in one dish? Does that need to be said?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about what the first case of the משנה means. Then it attacks that case as too obvious to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained the סיפא (which exempts) as one type of food eaten from two separate dishes, following the view that separate dishes divide. So the רישא (which obligates) must be one type in one dish. Two half-כזיתים of the same food in the same dish obviously combine, so why would the משנה bother teaching it?

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause of a משנה
does it need to be said? (meaning: it's obvious)

phrases.english: by inference, the first clause
phrases.notes: This follows from what we just said: the סיפא is about one type in two separate dishes.

phrases.english: is one type and one dish.
One type and one dish —
does that need to be said?!
phrases.notes: He isn't really asking; it's a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the משנה earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רישא of the משנה (two half-כזיתים, one type, one dish = liable)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the case is defined as one type in one dish, liability is obvious, so the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: רב הונא: there was awareness in between
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the person became aware of his sin between the two halves. The משנה follows רבן גמליאל, who holds that awareness does not split up half-measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What case are we dealing with here? One where he became aware in between the two halves. And the משנה follows רבן גמליאל, who said: Awareness does not count for half a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge. He changes the case so that the רישא teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, becoming aware of a sin (ידיעה) acts as a dividing line between sins. So you might think the two halves cannot join. רבן גמליאל holds that ידיעה about less than a full שיעור means nothing, because no קרבן is owed for it. So the halves still join, and that is the חידוש of the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here?
half of the required minimum amount

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, ידיעה between two half-שיעורים does not separate them, so they still combine to obligate a חטאת.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he had
awareness in between.
And it is Rabban Gamliel, who said:
There is no awareness for half a measure.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) and assigning it to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא is a plain case with nothing new, so it is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא includes ידיעה in between, and following רבן גמליאל the halves still combine.

steps.title: Dispute: two olive-amounts of forbidden fat, found out one at a time
steps.stepSummary: A person ate two כזיתים of חלב in one lapse of awareness, then found out about each one separately. רבי יוחנן says he brings two חטאות and ריש לקיש says only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Someone ate two olive-amounts of חלב in one lapse of awareness. He found out about the first, and later found out about the second. רבי יוחנן said: He brings two. ריש לקיש said: He brings only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a מחלוקת of אמוראים about whether separate moments of finding out create separate חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both כזיתים were eaten in one forgetting (העלם אחד), which usually means one חטאת. The new factor is that he found out about each one at a different time. רבי יוחנן holds the separate discoveries split it into two obligations. ריש לקיש holds it stays one.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree he ate everything in ONE העלם. The argument is only about what happens when he finds out at two different times.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat
in one lapse of awareness,
and became aware of the first,
and then became aware of the second.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: He is liable to bring two.
And Reish Lakish said:
He is liable to bring only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, related to the theme of ידיעה dividing sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: two חטאות. ריש לקיש: one חטאת.

steps.title: Each אמורא's source verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from 'על חטאתו... והביא' that each sin needs its own קרבן. ריש לקיש learns from 'מחטאתו ונסלח לו' that atoning for part of the sin forgives all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, from 'for his sin... and he shall bring.' ריש לקיש says he is exempt, from 'from his sin, and it shall be forgiven for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: Each אמורא brings a פסוק to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'על חטאתו' as 'for his (specific) sin': each sin he finds out about gets its own קרבן. ריש לקיש reads 'מחטאתו' as 'from (part of) his sin.' Even if the קרבן was brought for only part, the whole sin is forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: and it shall be forgiven for him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said he is liable:
"For his sin... and he shall bring."
And Reish Lakish said he is exempt:
"From his sin, and it shall be forgiven for him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for each side of the dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא ד: 'על חטאתו... והביא' versus 'מחטאתו ונסלח לו'

steps.title: Challenge to ריש לקיש from רבי יוחנן's verse
steps.stepSummary: How does ריש לקיש explain the פסוק 'על חטאתו... והביא'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש — isn't it written 'for his sin... and he shall bring'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with רבי יוחנן's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say that each sin needs its own קרבן. ריש לקיש has to explain what it means if he holds only one קרבן is needed.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish — isn't it written:
"For his sin... and he shall bring"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש using the opposing פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling of only one חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק implies a separate קרבן for each sin, which ריש לקיש seems to ignore.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: that verse is after atonement
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש applies 'על חטאתו' to a case where he found out about the second sin only after the first קרבן had already brought כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is about after atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש's answer narrows רבי יוחנן's פסוק to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first קרבן has already atoned, it is 'used up' and cannot cover a sin he discovers later. Then he needs a second קרבן. If he finds out before the כפרה, one קרבן covers both.

phrases.english: That is after atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על חטאתו' requires two קרבנות whenever there are two discoveries.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two קרבנות are needed only if the second discovery came after the first כפרה.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוחנן from ריש לקיש's verse
steps.stepSummary: How does רבי יוחנן explain 'מחטאתו ונסלח לו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן too — isn't it written 'from his sin, and it shall be forgiven for him'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around and asks רבי יוחנן about ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מחטאתו' suggests that atoning for part of a sin forgives the whole. That seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's two קרבנות.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan too — isn't it written:
"From his sin, and it shall be forgiven for him"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image challenge, now against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling of two חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'מחטאתו' implies partial atonement covers the whole sin, so one קרבן should be enough.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the verse is about a leftover half that doesn't combine
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, 'מחטאתו' is about someone who ate one and a half כזיתים and found out about one כזית. Then he ate another half during the forgetting of the leftover half. The פסוק teaches that the two halves do not join for a new חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? He ate one and a half כזיתים and found out about one כזית. Then he ate another half-כזית while still unaware of the second (leftover half). You might say the halves combine — so the פסוק teaches us they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by applying ריש לקיש's פסוק to a narrow, special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first leftover half-כזית was eaten together with the כזית he brought a קרבן for. So it was atoned 'מחטאתו', as part of that sin. Because it was already atoned, it cannot combine with the new half-כזית to make a new obligation. So the פסוק does not force one קרבן in the main case.

keyTerms.meaning: during the lapse of awareness of the second (half)

steps.whatToRemember: Each side reads the other's פסוק as a special case. ריש לקיש says 'על חטאתו' is after כפרה. רבי יוחנן says 'מחטאתו' teaches that an already-atoned half does not combine.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he ate an olive-bulk and a half,
and became aware of one olive-bulk,
and then ate another half olive-bulk
during the lapse of awareness of the second (half).
Lest you say they should combine —
it teaches us (that they do not).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל כְּזַיִת וּמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) for the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leftover half-כזית could join the new half to obligate a second חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leftover half was atoned as part of the first sin ('מחטאתו'), so it does not combine.

steps.title: רבינא's first option: they argue before designation
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether the dispute is when he found out before the הפרשה. If so, רבי יוחנן holds ידיעות divide and ריש לקיש holds הפרשות divide. After הפרשה, both agree he brings two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Do they argue when he found out before designating the animal? Then the argument is this: one holds discoveries divide, and the other holds designations divide. But after designation, ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן that he brings two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא begins a question about exactly when the מחלוקת applies. This is the first of three possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three stages: finding out (ידיעה), setting aside an animal (הפרשה), and offering it (כפרה). In this option, רבי יוחנן says the second discovery alone splits the sins. ריש לקיש needs a הפרשה in between. So if the second discovery came after הפרשה, even ריש לקיש says two.

keyTerms.meaning: designating an animal as the קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three stages: ידיעה (finding out), then הפרשה (setting aside the animal), then כפרה (offering it). Each option moves the dividing line to a different stage.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Do they disagree where he became aware before designation,
and this is what they disagree about:
that one master (R. Yoḥanan) holds awarenesses divide,
and one master (Reish Lakish) holds designations divide,
but after designation

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Reish Lakish agrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan
that he is liable to bring two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: דְּאִיתְיְדַע לֵיהּ קוֹדֶם הַפְרָשָׁה פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry into the exact scope of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At which stage (before or after הפרשה) do רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree?

steps.title: רבינא's second option: they argue after designation
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe they argue when he found out after the הפרשה. Then רבי יוחנן holds הפרשות divide and ריש לקיש holds only כפרות divide. Before הפרשה, both agree he brings one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps they argue when he found out after designation. Then one holds designations divide and the other holds atonements divide. But before designation, רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש that he brings only one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second possibility that moves the dispute one stage later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both agree that a discovery alone does not split the sins. רבי יוחנן needs a הפרשה in between, and ריש לקיש needs an actual כפרה, which fits his answer in step 6. So before הפרשה, everyone says one קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא דְּאִיתְיְדַע לֵיהּ לְאַחַר הַפְרָשָׁה פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Or perhaps they disagree where he became aware after designation,
and this is what they disagree about:
that one master (R. Yoḥanan) holds designations divide,
and one master (Reish Lakish) holds atonements divide.
But before designation

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan agrees with Reish Lakish
that he is liable to bring only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא דְּאִיתְיְדַע לֵיהּ לְאַחַר הַפְרָשָׁה פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second possible answer to the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מחלוקת is only after הפרשה, with agreement on one קרבן before it.

steps.title: רבינא's third option: they argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the מחלוקת applies both before and after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps they argue in both this case and that case?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers the third and last possibility, finishing his question. The next step gives רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this option, רבי יוחנן says discoveries already divide, so he says two even before הפרשה. ריש לקיש says only כפרה divides, so he says one even after הפרשה. That puts the dispute at both stages.

keyTerms.meaning: both in this (case) and in that

phrases.english: Or perhaps
in both this case and that case there is a dispute?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא בֵּין בָּזוֹ וּבֵין בָּזוֹ מַחֲלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third possible scope of the dispute, finishing רבינא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute covers both stages, before and after הפרשה.

steps.title: רב אשי answers that they argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers רבינא that it makes sense to say the מחלוקת applies both before and after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It makes sense that the dispute is in this case and in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the three-way question from Steps 9-11. He picks the third option: the dispute applies both before and after הפרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא offered three possibilities: the dispute is only before הפרשה, only after הפרשה, or in both. רב אשי chooses 'both' and says it is מסתברא, meaning it is logical. He will give the proof in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is logical
Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him: It is reasonable
that the dispute is both in this case and in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִסְתַּבְּרָא בֵּין בָּזוֹ וּבֵין בָּזוֹ מַחֲלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 9-11 by choosing the third option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does the מחלוקת apply: before הפרשה, after הפרשה, or both?

steps.title: Proof that they also argue after designation
steps.stepSummary: If ריש לקיש agreed that after הפרשה one brings two, he could have explained the פסוק as a case after הפרשה. He explained it as after כפרה instead, so he must disagree even after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think they argue only before הפרשה, and after הפרשה ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן that he brings two, then instead of setting the פסוק in a case after atonement, let him set it in a case after הפרשה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his first proof. He shows that ריש לקיש must disagree with רבי יוחנן even after הפרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש had to explain רבי יוחנן's פסוק 'על חטאתו... והביא', which suggests a second חטאת is sometimes needed. He placed it in a late, extreme case: after כפרה (Step 6). If he really agreed that two are needed already after הפרשה, he would have used that earlier and easier case. So in his view, even after הפרשה only one חטאת is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it should enter your mind (if you think)
Designating a specific animal as the קרבן
Atonement, which happens when the קרבן is actually brought
Rather than establishing it (applying it to a case)

steps.confusionAlert: Remember the order of events: first הפרשה (choosing the animal), and only later כפרה (bringing it). 'After כפרה' is a later point than 'after הפרשה'.

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind
that they disagree only before designation,
but after designation

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Reish Lakish agrees with Rabbi Yochanan
that he is liable to bring two —
then rather than establishing the verse as a case after atonement,
let him establish it as a case after designation!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ קוֹדֶם הַפְרָשָׁה פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer for the 'after הפרשה' side.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש disagrees even after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש chose to explain 'על חטאתו... והביא' as a case after כפרה, not after הפרשה.

steps.title: Proof that they also argue before designation
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן agreed that before הפרשה one brings only one, he could have explained the פסוק as a case before הפרשה. He explained it with a כזית and a half instead, so he must disagree even before הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they argue only after הפרשה, and before הפרשה רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש that he brings only one, then instead of setting the פסוק in a case of a כזית and a half, let him set it in a case before הפרשה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his second proof, the mirror image of the first. This time he shows that רבי יוחנן must disagree even before הפרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן needed the פסוק 'מחטאתו' to teach a case where only one חטאת is brought. He gave it an unusual case: a כזית and a half (Step 8). If he agreed that before הפרשה only one is brought, he could have used that simpler case. So he must hold that two are brought even before הפרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: He is liable for only one (one קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's logic: each אמורא picked a harder explanation of the פסוק when an easier one was available. That shows each one disagrees in the other's 'easy' case, so the מחלוקת exists both before and after הפרשה.

phrases.english: And if they disagree only after designation,
but before designation

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan agrees with Reish Lakish
that he is liable to bring only one,
then rather than establishing the verse as a case of an olive-bulk and a half,
let him establish it as a case before designation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel proof for the 'before הפרשה' side, completing רב אשי's argument.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן disagrees even before הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן chose to explain 'מחטאתו' as a case of a כזית and a half, not as a case before הפרשה.

steps.title: Maybe the explanations were only given as 'if you say'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Perhaps the matter was in doubt, and each explanation of the פסוק was given only for one side of that doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he was unsure, and he spoke in the style of 'if you wish to say': If you say they argue before הפרשה, how does רבי יוחנן explain the פסוק? With a כזית and a half. And if you say they argue after הפרשה, how does ריש לקיש explain the פסוק? As after כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב אשי's proof. Each explanation of the פסוק may have been said only for one possible side of the doubt, so the explanations prove nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, רבי יוחנן's 'כזית and a half' explanation was meant only for the possibility that the dispute is before הפרשה. In that scenario he cannot use 'before הפרשה', because there he disagrees. Likewise ריש לקיש's 'after כפרה' explanation was meant only for the possibility that the dispute is after הפרשה. Neither explanation shows that the dispute exists in both cases, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: He was truly in doubt about it
If you wish to say (a conditional, 'what-if' answer)
How does he establish (explain) the verse?

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say רב אשי is wrong about the law. It only says his proof does not work. The answer could still be 'both', but it is not proven.
steps.whatToRemember: The ראיה from how each side explained the פסוק fails. Those explanations could be conditional 'if you say' answers given while the matter was still in doubt.

phrases.english: how does Rabbi Yochanan establish the verse? —
As a case of an olive-bulk and a half.
And if you wish to say

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the conclusion that the dispute applies in both cases.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The explanations of the פסוק may have been conditional answers given under a doubt, so they cannot show what each אמורא holds in the other scenario.

steps.title: עולא begins a statement about the definite guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: עולא opens a new teaching: according to the view that an אשם ודאי does not require knowledge of the sin at the outset... (the statement continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: According to the one who says that an אשם ודאי does not require knowledge at the beginning,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new statement by עולא about אשם ודאי. This line only sets up his rule; the rest of it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with חטאת, which is brought only after the person knows he sinned. עולא now turns to אשם ודאי, the definite guilt-offering brought for things like robbery, מעילה, or relations with a שפחה חרופה. He starts from the view that this קרבן does not need prior knowledge of the sin, and he will draw a consequence from that view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
A definite guilt-offering (for robbery, מעילה, or שפחה חרופה)
Knowledge of the sin at the outset

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that ידיעה can divide sins into separate קרבנות drove the whole dispute above. עולא now asks how this works for a קרבן that does not need ידיעה at all.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
According to the one who says that a definite guilt-offering
does not require knowledge at the outset,
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.
